event: During the second act, Pearl watches Colette's throat from the prompt-side wing.
Colette sings her solo lit gold under the gels, chin tipped back, her neck taut and luminous.
Pearl loves her for her beauty, and aches to have it off Colette and onto herself.
Pearl tells the reader they may stop reading now; they will learn nothing kinder.
Kit on her shoulder, needle threaded from an act-one hem emergency, she lets herself be happy.
Everyone trusts sweet Pearl, the wardrobe assistant who means every compliment she gives.
She never lies about loving them; she only keeps quiet that she means to take it.
Pearl chose her own name at sixteen, shedding her mother's soft forgettable one.
She tells how a pearl is made: shine built layer on layer over a speck of filth.
She always meant to become that, and tonight the world has handed her the tools.
During the bows, Mr. Aldous, who funds half the season, finds her in the wing.
He presses a glass of something gold into her hand that she never asked for.
He calls hers the only honest face back here; she says she wants everyone wonderful.
She touches his sleeve, he glows, and she admires his magnificent watch.
The System rates her Allure 14.0, where ordinary is 10.0; doors open for her.
Aldous wanders off to be wonderful at someone else, and Pearl drinks his gold drink.
Colette finishes her final bow, and the house comes up roaring.
Pearl warns that in about forty minutes she will kill Colette, and wants her known first.
Colette carries her beauty like weather; Pearl is pretty the way a knife is.
Colette's Celerity lets her change shape in the air; Pearl's is 11.0, a girl hurrying.
Offstage, Colette sees Tamsin, a terrified first-season corps girl, crying in the far wing.
Colette crosses the backstage, takes Tamsin's wet face in her hands, and makes her laugh.
She tells her a cue light dead since intermission made her miss her entrance, not her.
Colette reads rooms like sheet music and sees everyone, but never once sees Pearl.
Within twenty minutes the company drains out into the cold, and the work-lights come down.
Colette takes Pearl to the mirrored studio off the green room to break down her costume.
Pearl says she planned nothing tonight: no knife, no scheme, only a sewing kit.
Among a hundred reflections, she works the bodice hooks down Colette's spine.
Colette tells Pearlie she should be dancing, with a better line than her own.
As Colette's throat works around the words, a lens drops over Pearl's eye.
She can taste Colette: sweet beauty, bright humming quickness, a cool minty seeing.
A calm, total certainty comes over her: she could just take it.
Pearl is delighted: she always could, she only lacked the hands.
She feels no dread, only the giddy fizz of a child at the top of the high board.
Her French-forged wardrobe shears sit in the kit at her hip.
The lens tells her she may keep only one thing: one deliberate theft per life.
She knows then that she will be very, very good at this.
Colette chatters about the spring program, arms lifted, throat tipped back and trusting.
Pearl says, "Colette."
Colette meets Pearl's eyes in the mirror and, for a quarter of a second, finally sees her.
Pearl smiles at her, and means it.
Watching in the glass, Pearl cuts Colette's throat with the shears, fast as a change in the air.
Red sheets down the gold-lit cream; Pearl thinks they never looked so good together.
A click like a key turning in a lock, and the lens opens all the way.
Colette, slumped and quiet in Pearl's arms, stops being a person and becomes a display.
A frost-bright card appraises the three best things Colette ever was.
Kneeling in the red, grinning, Pearl reads the card like a love letter.
The hard part is the choosing: she may take exactly one home, and the rest is lost.
Appraisal of Colette Vane, unpowered; Pearl: Might 8, Vit 9, Cel 11, Acu 12, Will 10, Allure 14.
Offered: Allure 16.0 (14.0 to 15.6), Celerity 15.0 (11.0 to 12.5), Acuity 13.0 (12.0 to 13.3).
The card says: select one, one only.
Pearl crouches beside Colette and lets her eyes wander the menu only she can see.
One of the three doors glows brighter than its neighbours.
Her finger hovers over the light; this will be the best part of her life, every time.
